data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"Resumption is safe iff the last committed entry that has full event framing (delimiters, checksum, causal fingerprint) is a complete event whose fingerprint matches the expected continuation point; any partial trailing fragment from mid-stream exhaustion is definitionally a non-event under append-only semantics and cannot corrupt event identity. Resumption must be refused when the last byte-stream boundary is ambiguous such that a partial fragment could be mistaken for a complete event.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the event framing protocol is self-delimiting but lacks integrity checking, a partial fragment could be misinterpreted as a complete event by a naive reader, corrupting identity.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If downstream consumers already advanced state based on a speculative read of the partial fragment before exhaustion was detected, the corruption is in derived state, not the log, and log-level resumption alone cannot repair it.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the causal fingerprint of the last complete event does not match the expected continuation (e.g., another writer appended between exhaustion and resumption), resumption must be refused regardless of framing.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the append-only medium does not support atomic write units smaller than a full event, a partial fragment may have overwritten or interleaved with a prior complete event's tail, corrupting identity.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Append-only identity attaches to complete, framed events, not to raw byte sequences. A partial fragment left by token-budget exhaustion lacks the closing delimiter and/or checksum that confer event status. The resumption protocol reads backward from the end of the log, verifies framing integrity, and quarantines (ignores) any trailing non-framed bytes. Because no event identity was ever assigned to those bytes, ignoring them does not modify, delete, or rewrite any recorded event\u2014append-only integrity is preserved. Refusal is warranted only when the framing protocol cannot distinguish partial from complete (e.g., length-prefix without checksum and the fragment happens to contain a spurious length field).","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
